qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Anthony Smith (The Left) Subject:

On 22 October 2026, Law No 32743 granted Keiko Fujimori’s government a 90-day window to issue legislative decrees on intelligence, geolocation, criminal justice and the prison system, in particular as regards the detention of adolescents. Meanwhile, the extension of the state of emergency in Lima and Callao allows for restrictions to be imposed on people’s freedom of assembly and movement, personal liberty and their right to the inviolability of their homes. Under the guise of combating crime, this over-centralisation of exceptional powers poses a threat to fundamental freedoms and the balance of powers, despite the safeguards formally enshrined in Peruvian law. Respect for democracy, human rights and the rule of law are established as an essential element of the EU-Colombia-Peru-Ecuador Trade Agreement under Article 1, however. 1.
Has the Vice-President / High Representative asked the Peruvian Government for verifiable safeguards regarding the oversight of these exceptional powers and respect for fundamental freedoms?
If these safeguards are not respected, under what conditions will it propose appropriate measures – such as a suspension – under Article 8(3) of the trade agreement?
